default.p.test-53-p1.vietnamese: Japan is currently facing a declining birth rate. The total fertility rate, meaning the number of children a woman gives birth to over her lifetime, was quite low at 1.39 in 2010. In addition, married couples actually had an average of 1.77 children, but the ideal number of children they considered was 3. When wives in couples whose expected number of children was lower than their ideal number were asked why, the most common reasons included: 1. Raising and educating children is too expensive, 2. They are reluctant to have children at an older age, 3. They cannot bear the burden of caring for children, and 4. Having children interferes with their work. Even survey data from the Cabinet Office show that people’s attitudes toward children differ considerably depending on their age.

default.q.test-24-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 海外旅行すると会社がお金を払ってくれる。
The company offers a company-funded overseas travel benefit, with all expenses covered (全額会社持ち). This matches the statement that the company pays when an employee travels abroad.
default.q.test-24-q1-1.explanation: The exact basis for the question is the quotation: 「全額会社持ちの海外社員旅行。」, meaning “an overseas company trip for employees, fully paid for by the company.” The key point is the suffix 「〜持ち」, derived from 持つ (“to bear” or “take responsibility”), which follows a noun referring to a person or organization to indicate who pays the expenses. It commonly conveys full financial coverage or sponsorship in everyday and business contexts. Therefore, 「全額会社持ち」 is equivalent to the wording in choice (d): 「海外旅行すると会社がお金を払ってくれる」. To avoid the distractor in choice (a), note that the passage says 「基本賃金は下がらない」 (the base wage does not decrease), but it also says 「手当は減る」 (allowances decrease). Therefore, the total income (給料) of people in their 60s and 70s cannot be the same.
default.q.test-24-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that after age 60, the allowance decreases (手当は減る) even though the base salary remains unchanged. Therefore, the total salaries of people aged 60 and 70 cannot be the same.
default.q.test-24-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) This is incorrect because the company’s childcare leave (育児休暇) lasts only 3 years, not 4 years.
default.q.test-24-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) This is incorrect because the company states that there is no overtime (残業はない) and that the workday is 7 hours and 15 minutes; there is no rule requiring a fine for working 9 hours.
default.q.test-24-q1-1.why.3: ✓ (d) Correct because the company provides an overseas trip for employees and covers the entire cost (全額会社持ちの海外社員旅行).
default.q.test-3-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) ろうかで携帯電話を使うこと
By elimination, choices (a), (b), and (d) directly violate the hospital’s prohibitions. Therefore, using a mobile phone outside the hospital room, as stated in choice (c), is the only permissible action.
default.q.test-3-q1-1.explanation: The key N2 grammar point in the passage is the pattern 「V-ru / Nの + 恐れがある」(there is a risk that..., there is a possibility of...), which has a formal warning tone and is used for a potentially negative event in a public or medical context. The essential evidence comes from the original sentence:「携帯電話は（注）医療機器に悪い影響を与える恐れがありますので、病室では電源を切ってください。」(Because mobile phones may adversely affect medical equipment, please turn them off in patient rooms.) For easily confused answer choices, pay attention to 「〜以下」, which includes the stated threshold and everything below it, eliminating option (b) because a five-year-old falls under「小学生以下」. The phrase「すべて禁止」also immediately rules out smoking in the lounge in option (d). For questions asking what is possible (できること), systematically eliminate actions prohibited by expressions such as「できません」and「禁止」. This leaves using a phone outside the patient room in option (c) as the only acceptable choice.
default.q.test-3-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The passage clearly states that visitors may not eat or drink in the hospital room (病室内では飲んだり食べたりできません), so they may not give the patient fruit there.
default.q.test-3-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) A five-year-old falls under 小学生以下 (elementary school age or younger), so under the regulations, children in this age group are strictly not allowed to visit patients.
default.q.test-3-q1-1.why.2: ✓ (c) After eliminating the other three choices because they directly violate the prohibitions, using a phone outside the hospital room is the only permissible action.
default.q.test-3-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) Smoking and drinking are prohibited throughout the hospital premises (病院内はすべて禁止), including the lounge area.
default.q.test-4-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) 一番効果があるのは自動車を使わないことである。
Among the listed energy-saving measures, not using a car—taking a train, riding a bicycle, or walking—reduces CO2 emissions by up to 400 g per day. This is the largest reduction among the measures and therefore the most effective.
default.q.test-4-q1-1.explanation: The passage uses the N2 pattern「〜ものの」(V/adjective in plain form + ものの, meaning “although...”) to describe a result contrary to expectations in the following clause: many people try it but often give up because it is troublesome. It is combined with the gentle suggestion pattern「〜たらどうですか」(“why don’t you try...?”). The decisive evidence is the sentence:「自動車を使わず電車、自転車、徒歩にすれば４００ｇ減らせる。」(“If you use trains, bicycles, or walk instead of using a car, you can reduce it by 400 g.”). Compared with the other figures in the passage—avoiding plastic bags (42 g), turning off the TV (45 g), turning off the shower (86 g), sorting waste (119 g), and keeping heating below 20 degrees (129 g)—400 g is the largest amount and corresponds to「一番効果がある」(the most effective). In reading comprehension, watch out for the exaggeration trap in choice (c), which claims that the entire problem can be solved, and the incorrect causal relationship in choice (d): the author only emphasizes「結果が目に見えれば頑張れる」(“if the results are visible, we can stay motivated”), not that calculating the amount directly reduces emissions.
default.q.test-4-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The passage only advises people to try calculating the amount of emissions they can reduce; it does not claim that those making an effort monitor the figures every day.
default.q.test-4-q1-1.why.1: ✓ (b) Among the listed actions, not using a car reduces CO2 emissions by up to 400 g per day, far more than the other actions (42–129 g). Therefore, it has the greatest effect.
default.q.test-4-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) The author merely lists things individuals can do to help prevent global warming and does not claim that carrying out all of them would completely stop the problem.
default.q.test-4-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) Calculating the figures is only a method that helps people see concrete results and gain motivation to make an effort. The act of calculating itself does not directly reduce emissions.
default.q.test-5-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) Ｂ
The buyer wants an electronic dictionary with audio playback at the lowest possible price. After eliminating A, which cannot play audio, B is the most economical option among the remaining choices.
default.q.test-5-q1-1.explanation: The passage identifies two essential buyer criteria in the quotation: 「Ａ以外は音を聞くことができます。音が聞けてなるべく経済的な辞書が買いたいです。」 (Except for A, all of them allow the user to listen to the audio. I want to buy a dictionary that has audio and is as economical as possible.) Grammatically, 「N + 以外」excludes the preceding item from the set, while the adverb「なるべく」(as much as possible) modifies the na-adjective「経済的」(economical, cost-effective) to express a desire to optimize the price. Since the first requirement is「音が聞けて」, dictionary A is immediately eliminated because it has no audio. To avoid the trap, first use「以外」to exclude A, then apply the criterion「なるべく経済的」: among the audio models B, C, and D, model B is the most economical.
default.q.test-5-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) Type A does not meet the requirement because it cannot produce sound; the statement says that all types except A can produce sound.
default.q.test-5-q1-1.why.1: ✓ (b) Model B perfectly meets both conditions: it produces sound and is the most economical, least expensive option among the models with sound.
default.q.test-5-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) Although Type C has audio functions, it is not the most cost-effective choice compared with Type B.
default.q.test-5-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) Type D can be heard, but it costs more, so it does not meet the top priority of keeping the budget low.
default.q.test-50-q2-2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) Receiving the lowest weekly pay
Yeon prioritizes studying to maintain the scholarship and cannot work late or leave the magic club. Therefore, he accepts the lowest weekly pay as long as it is enough to cover the 10,000-yen living expense.
default.q.test-50-q2-2.explanation: The key point in the passage is the adverbial grammar pattern 「なるべく」 used with the negative form 「〜ないで」 in the quoted sentence 「ですからなるべく働かないで勉強に時間を使いたいです」 (So I want to work as little as possible and use my time for studying), expressing the speaker's intention to minimize part-time work in order to prioritize maintaining the grades needed for a scholarship. Alongside this, the conditional pattern 「〜ば」 in 「奨学金をもらっているので週に1万円あれば生活できます」 (Since I receive a scholarship, I can live if I have 10,000 yen a week) indicates the minimum necessary condition, showing that Yeon is willing to choose a job with fewer hours and accept the lowest pay as long as it covers living expenses. Therefore, the only disadvantage of the job Yeon chose is that it provides the least weekly income compared with the other jobs. To distinguish easily confused choices, learners must clearly separate a condition that rules something out from the beginning from a disadvantage of the selected job: choices (c) and (d) are things Yeon firmly refuses, as shown by 「マジックは止めたくないです」 (I do not want to give up magic) and 「夜中の仕事は次の日の授業に影響しますからできません」 (I cannot do night work because it affects the next day's classes). Thus, they cannot describe the job Yeon chose.
default.q.test-50-q2-2.why.0: ✓ (a) Yeon needs only 10,000 yen per week for living expenses and wants to devote as much time as possible to studying in order to keep the scholarship, so he accepts the job with the lowest weekly income.
default.q.test-50-q2-2.why.1: ✗ (b) Having a schedule every day is not a disadvantage of the chosen job, and the passage does not say that the job keeps him busy all week.
default.q.test-50-q2-2.why.2: ✗ (c) The passage clearly states that Yeon does not want to quit the magic club (「マジックは止めたくないです」). Therefore, the job he chooses must not interfere with this interest.
default.q.test-50-q2-2.why.3: ✗ (d) Yeon clearly stated that he cannot work at night because it would affect his classes the next day (“夜中の仕事は次の日の授業に影響しますからできません”), so he would not choose a job that would make him sleepy during class.
